label: lem:Fejer
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:Fejer}
	Let $S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m$ be nonempty, and let
	$\{x_k\}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m$ be Fej\'er monotone with respect to $S$,
	that is,
	\begin{equation*}
		\|x_{k+1}-x\|\le\|x_k-x\|,
		\qquad
		\forall x\in S,\quad k\ge0.
	\end{equation*}
	If every accumulation point of $\{x_k\}$ belongs to $S$, then
	$\{x_k\}$ converges to a point in $S$.

title: Proof
body_md:
The first candidate in \eqref{eq:aeg-vr-stepsize} gives
	$\lambda_{k+1}\le(1+\eta_k)\lambda_k$ pathwise. Hence the proof of
	\eqref{eq:vr-lambda-upper} is identical to that of Lemma~\ref{lem31}.
	Also,
	\begin{equation*}
		(\lambda_{k+1}-\lambda_k)_+\le\bar\lambda\eta_k.
	\end{equation*}
	Since $\sum_k\eta_k<\infty$, the positive variations $(\lambda_{k+1}-\lambda_k)_+$ are summable
	pathwise. The identity
	\begin{equation*}
		\lambda_{N+1}-\lambda_0=
		\sum_{k=0}^{N}(\lambda_{k+1}-\lambda_k)_+
		-\sum_{k=0}^{N}(\lambda_{k+1}-\lambda_k)_-
	\end{equation*}
	and $\lambda_{N+1}\ge0$ imply summability of the negative variations.
	This proves \eqref{eq:vr-lambda-variation}, and therefore
	$\{\lambda_k\}$ is Cauchy and convergent. The expectation bounds in
	\eqref{eq:vr-lambda-variation-expectation} follow from the same deterministic
	majorants and Tonelli's theorem.

label: eq:vr-projection-split
title: Proof
body_md:
Fix any $t^*\in U^*$ and $k\ge1$. Since
	$t^{k+1}=P_U\left(\bar t^k-\lambda_k\widehat F_k\right)$, 
	the inequality \eqref{2.2} gives
	\begin{align*}
		\|t^{k+1}-t^*\|^2
		\le{}&\|\bar t^k-t^*\|^2
		-\|t^{k+1}-\bar t^k\|^2+2\lambda_k
		\langle \widehat F_k,t^*-t^{k+1}\rangle.
	\end{align*}
	Splitting $t^*-t^{k+1}=t^*-t^{k+\frac12}+t^{k+\frac12}-t^{k+1}$,	we obtain
	\begin{align}
		\|t^{k+1}-t^*\|^2
		\le{}&\|\bar t^k-t^*\|^2
		-\|t^{k+1}-\bar t^k\|^2-2\lambda_k
		\langle t^{k+\frac12}-t^*,\widehat F_k\rangle
		+2\lambda_k\langle\widehat F_k,t^{k+\frac12}-t^{k+1}\rangle.
		\label{eq:vr-projection-split}
	\end{align}
	Applying \eqref{2.1} with	$u=t^{k+1}\in U$ and $v=\bar t^k-\lambda_kF(s^k)$ yields
	\begin{equation*}
		\left\langle
		\bar t^k-\lambda_kF(s^k)-t^{k+\frac12},
		t^{k+1}-t^{k+\frac12}
		\right\rangle
		\le0.
	\end{equation*}
	Equivalently,
	\begin{equation*}\label{eq:vr-prediction-optimality}
		\lambda_k\left\langle F(s^k),t^{k+\frac12}-t^{k+1}\right\rangle
		\le\left\langle\bar t^k-t^{k+\frac12},t^{k+\frac12}-t^{k+1}\right\rangle.
	\end{equation*}
	Using
	$\widehat F_k=F(s^k)+F_{\xi_k}(t^{k+\frac12})-F_{\xi_k}(s^k)$, it follows that
	\begin{align*}
		\lambda_k\langle\widehat F_k,t^{k+\frac12}-t^{k+1}\rangle
		\le&\left\langle\bar t^k-t^{k+\frac12},
		t^{k+\frac12}-t^{k+1}\right\rangle
		+\lambda_k\left\langle
		F_{\xi_k}(t^{k+\frac12})-F_{\xi_k}(s^k),
		t^{k+\frac12}-t^{k+1}\right\rangle.
	\end{align*}
	Substituting this estimate into
	\eqref{eq:vr-projection-split} and using the identity
	\begin{align*}
		&-\|t^{k+1}-\bar t^k\|^2+
		2\left\langle\bar t^k-t^{k+\frac12},t^{k+\frac12}-t^{k+1}\right\rangle
		=-\|t^{k+1}-t^{k+\frac12}\|^2
		-\|\bar t^k-t^{k+\frac12}\|^2,
	\end{align*}
	we obtain
	\begin{align}
		\|t^{k+1}-t^*\|^2
		\le{}&\|\bar t^k-t^*\|^2
		-\|t^{k+1}-t^{k+\frac12}\|^2
		-\|\bar t^k-t^{k+\frac12}\|^2
		\notag\\
		&-2\lambda_k\left\langle
		t^{k+\frac12}-t^*,\widehat F_k\right\rangle
		+2\lambda_k\left\langle
		F_{\xi_k}(t^{k+\frac12})-F_{\xi_k}(s^k),
		t^{k+\frac12}-t^{k+1}\right\rangle.
		\label{eq:vr-before-young}
	\end{align}
	By Young's inequality,
	\begin{equation*}
		2\lambda_k\left\langle
		F_{\xi_k}(t^{k+\frac12})-F_{\xi_k}(s^k),
		t^{k+\frac12}-t^{k+1}\right\rangle
		\le\beta\|t^{k+1}-t^{k+\frac12}\|^2
		+\frac{\lambda_k^2}{\beta}\|F_{\xi_k}(t^{k+\frac12})-F_{\xi_k}(s^k)\|^2.
	\end{equation*}
	Therefore,
	\begin{align}
		\|t^{k+1}-t^*\|^2
		\le{}&\|\bar t^k-t^*\|^2
		-(1-\beta)\|t^{k+1}-t^{k+\frac12}\|^2
		-\|\bar t^k-t^{k+\frac12}\|^2
		\notag\\
		&-2\lambda_k\left\langle
		t^{k+\frac12}-t^*,\widehat F_k\right\rangle
		+\frac{\lambda_k^2}{\beta}\|F_{\xi_k}(t^{k+\frac12})-F_{\xi_k}(s^k)\|^2.
		\label{eq:vr-after-young}
	\end{align}
	Since $\bar t^k=\beta t^k+(1-\beta)s^k$, the standard convex-combination identity gives, for every $u\in\mathbb R^m$,
	\begin{equation*}
		\|\bar t^k-u\|^2=\beta\|t^k-u\|^2
		+(1-\beta)\|s^k-u\|^2
		-\beta(1-\beta)\|t^k-s^k\|^2.
	\end{equation*}
	Applying this identity with $u=t^*$ and
	$u=t^{k+\frac12}$, and subtracting the resulting equalities, yields
	\begin{align*}
		\|\bar t^k-t^*\|^2
		-\|\bar t^k-t^{k+\frac12}\|^2
		={}&\beta\|t^k-t^*\|^2
		+(1-\beta)\|s^k-t^*\|^2\\
		&-\beta\|t^k-t^{k+\frac12}\|^2
		-(1-\beta)\|s^k-t^{k+\frac12}\|^2.
	\end{align*}
	Substituting this equality into
	\eqref{eq:vr-after-young} gives
	\begin{align}
		\|t^{k+1}-t^*\|^2
		\le{}&\beta\|t^k-t^*\|^2
		+(1-\beta)\|s^k-t^*\|^2
		-2\lambda_k\left\langle
		t^{k+\frac12}-t^*,\widehat F_k\right\rangle
		\notag\\
		&-(1-\beta)
		\|t^{k+1}-t^{k+\frac12}\|^2
		-(1-\beta)\|s^k-t^{k+\frac12}\|^2
		-\beta\|t^k-t^{k+\frac12}\|^2
		\notag\\
		&+\frac{\lambda_k^2}{\beta}\|F_{\xi_k}(t^{k+\frac12})-F_{\xi_k}(s^k)\|^2.
		\label{eq:vr-prelocal}
	\end{align}
	
	
	
	We next control the last term. By the second candidate in
	\eqref{eq:aeg-vr-stepsize},
	\begin{equation*}
		\frac{\lambda_{k+1}^2}{\beta}
		\|F_{\xi_k}(t^{k+\frac12})-F_{\xi_k}(s^k)\|^2
		\le\beta\|t^{k+\frac12}-s^k\|^2.
	\end{equation*}
	Using $\lambda_k^2\le\lambda_{k+1}^2+2\lambda_k(\lambda_k-\lambda_{k+1})_+$, we have
	\begin{align}
		\frac{\lambda_k^2}{\beta}
		\|F_{\xi_k}(t^{k+\frac12})-F_{\xi_k}(s^k)\|^2
		\le{}&\beta\|t^{k+\frac12}-s^k\|^2
		+\frac{2\lambda_k}{\beta}
		\|F_{\xi_k}(t^{k+\frac12})-F_{\xi_k}(s^k)\|^2
		(\lambda_k-\lambda_{k+1})_+.
		\label{eq:vr-error-split}
	\end{align}
	Since $s^k\in U$,	nonexpansiveness of $P_U$, \eqref{eq:snapshot-gap}, and
	\eqref{eq:stochastic-operator-control} yield
	\begin{align}
		\|t^{k+\frac12}-s^k\|
		&=\left\|P_U\!\left(\bar t^k-\lambda_kF(s^k)\right)-P_U(s^k)\right\|
		\notag\\
		&\le\beta\|t^k-s^k\|+\lambda_k\|F(s^k)\|
		\notag\\
		&\le\beta w+\lambda_k\max_{i\in[N]}\|F_i(s^k)\|
		\notag\\
		&\le\beta w+\sqrt{\bar\lambda}=R.
		\label{eq:vr-prediction-gap}
	\end{align}
	If $\alpha\in(0,1)$, by
	Assumption~\ref{ass4}, Proposition~\ref{pro3.1}, and
	\eqref{eq:vr-prediction-gap},
	\begin{align*}
		&\sqrt{\frac{2\lambda_k}{\beta}}\,
		\|F_{\xi_k}(t^{k+\frac12})-F_{\xi_k}(s^k)\|\\
		&\quad\le\sqrt{\frac{2}{\beta}}\,
		\|t^{k+\frac12}-s^k\|
		\Bigl[\sqrt{\lambda_k}
		\left(K_0+K_2\|t^{k+\frac12}-s^k\|^{\frac{\alpha}{1-\alpha}}\right)
		+K_1\sqrt{\lambda_k}\,\|F_{\xi_k}(s^k)\|^\alpha\Bigr]\\
		&\quad\le\sqrt{\frac{2}{\beta}}\,R
		\left[\sqrt{\bar\lambda}
		\left(K_0+K_2R^{\frac{\alpha}{1-\alpha}}\right)
		+\bar\lambda^{\frac{1-\alpha}{2}}K_1\right].
	\end{align*}
	If $\alpha=1$, Proposition~\ref{pro3.1} similarly gives
	\begin{align*}
		&\sqrt{\frac{2\lambda_k}{\beta}}\,
		\|F_{\xi_k}(t^{k+\frac12})-F_{\xi_k}(s^k)\|
		\le\sqrt{\frac{2}{\beta}}\,R
		\left(\sqrt{\bar\lambda}L_0+L_1\right)e^{L_1R},
	\end{align*}
	where we used $\sqrt{\lambda_k}\|F_{\xi_k}(s^k)\|
	\le1$. Thus, in both cases, by the definition of $\bar M$,
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:vr-component-bound}
		\frac{2\lambda_k}{\beta}
		\|F_{\xi_k}(t^{k+\frac12})-F_{\xi_k}(s^k)\|^2
		\le\bar M.
	\end{equation}
	Combining \eqref{eq:vr-error-split} and
	\eqref{eq:vr-component-bound} gives
	\begin{align*}
		\frac{\lambda_k^2}{\beta}
		\|F_{\xi_k}(t^{k+\frac12})-F_{\xi_k}(s^k)\|^2
		\le&\beta\|t^{k+\frac12}-s^k\|^2
		+\bar M(\lambda_k-\lambda_{k+1})_+.
	\end{align*}
	Substituting this estimate into \eqref{eq:vr-prelocal} yields
	\begin{align*}
		\|t^{k+1}-t^*\|^2
		\le{}&\beta\|t^k-t^*\|^2
		+(1-\beta)\|s^k-t^*\|^2-2\lambda_k
		\langle t^{k+\frac12}-t^*,\widehat F_k\rangle\\
		&-(1-\beta)\|t^{k+1}-t^{k+\frac12}\|^2
		-(1-2\beta)\|s^k-t^{k+\frac12}\|^2
		-\beta\|t^k-t^{k+\frac12}\|^2\\
		&+\bar M(\lambda_k-\lambda_{k+1})_+.
	\end{align*}
	
	Finally, taking conditional expectation with respect to
	$\mathcal F_k$, using \eqref{eq:svrg-unbiased}, gives
	\begin{equation*}
		-\mathbb E_k
		\langle t^{k+\frac12}-t^*,\widehat F_k\rangle
		=-\langle t^{k+\frac12}-t^*,F(t^{k+\frac12})\rangle
		\le-\mu\operatorname{dist}^p(t^{k+\frac12},U^*),
	\end{equation*}
	where the last inequality is due to $p$-quasi-sharpness.
	Substituting this inequality into the preceding estimate proves
	\eqref{eq:vr-one-step}.

label: th41
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{th41}
	Suppose Assumptions~\ref{ass1}--\ref{ass4} hold, let the iterates be
	generated by Algorithm~\ref{alg4}, and assume \eqref{eq:w-condition} holds.
	Then the following statements hold.
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item[$\mathbf{(i)}$]
		For every $t^*\in U^*$, the sequence
		\begin{equation*}
			\Phi_k(t^*):=\beta\|t^k-t^*\|^2
			+\frac{1-\beta}{P_1}\|s^k-t^*\|^2
		\end{equation*}
		is bounded and converges almost surely.
		
		\item[$\mathbf{(ii)}$]
		The stepsizes are bounded away from zero almost surely: \begin{equation}\label{eq:vr-lambda-lower}
			\lambda_k\ge\underline{\lambda}>0,
			\qquad k\ge0,
		\end{equation}
		where
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:vr-lambda-lower-def}
			\underline{\lambda}=
			\begin{cases}
				\displaystyle
				\min\left\{\lambda_0,\,\lambda_1,\,
				\frac{\beta}{K_0+K_1H_1^\alpha+K_2(\beta w+\sqrt{\bar\lambda})^{\frac{\alpha}{1-\alpha}}},\,
				\frac{1}{H_1^2}\right\},
				& \alpha\in(0,1),\\[4mm]
				\displaystyle
				\min\left\{\lambda_0,\,\lambda_1,\,
				\frac{\beta}{(L_0+L_1H_1)
					e^{L_1(\beta w+\sqrt{\bar\lambda})}},\,
				\frac{1}{H_1^2}\right\},
				& \alpha=1.
			\end{cases}
		\end{equation}
		where $H_1:=\sup_{k\ge0}\max_{i\in[N]}\|F_i(s^k)\|<\infty$  almost surely, and $1/H_1^2=+\infty$ if $H_1=0$; any candidate with a zero denominator is interpreted as
		$+\infty$.
		
		
		\item[$\mathbf{(iii)}$]
		There exists a $U^*$-valued random variable $\bar t$ such that
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:vr-as-convergence}
			t^k\to\bar t,
			\qquad
			s^k\to\bar t
			\qquad\text{almost surely}.
		\end{equation}
	\end{enumerate}

title: Remark
body_md:
The rates in Theorem~\ref{th43} concern the expected
	infimum of the Lyapunov function. They also imply the corresponding
	expected squared-distance rates because, for every $k$,
	\begin{equation*}
		\beta\,\operatorname{dist}^2(t^k,U^*)
		\le \inf_{u^*\in U^*}\Phi_k(u^*),
		\qquad
		\frac{1-\beta}{P_1}\,\operatorname{dist}^2(s^k,U^*)
		\le \inf_{u^*\in U^*}\Phi_k(u^*).
	\end{equation*}
